key_insight: A PPO-based controller can coordinate battery, hydrogen, diesel, and grid exchange in a community microgrid to maximize revenue while maintaining very high load satisfaction under uncertainty.
engineering_relevance: The work shows how reinforcement learning can improve operational scheduling of hybrid renewable microgrids, especially where storage coupling and variable prices make rule-based control inefficient.
method: Formulated EMS as an 11-state Markov decision process
Used PPO with three continuous actions for battery, diesel, and hydrogen dispatch
Evaluated grid-connected operation with PV, wind, battery, electrolyzer, H2 storage, fuel cell, and diesel backup
evidence_signal: The policy was tested on 8,760 hourly observations for a 1,000-household community and achieved A$195,690.67 annual operating revenue, 91.2% renewable fraction, and 99.77% load satisfaction in the base case.
watch_item: Performance is sensitive to renewable-profile variability and training stability, so real deployment would need robust retraining and careful validation across operating boundaries.
paper_title: Deep Reinforcement Learning-Based Energy Management for Hydrogen-Enabled Community Microgrids Under Uncertainty
